pages.title: Video Screen
pages.text: $(warn)Requires NarutoLoading.$()$(br2)Drag a video file onto a group of adjacent item frames to create a live $(bold)video screen$() in the world. Video decoding and playback are handled by NarutoLoading's built-in FFmpeg engine.

pages.title: How to Use
pages.text: $(bold)1.$() Arrange adjacent item frames all facing the same direction (e.g. a 4×3 grid on a wall).$(br2)$(bold)2.$() Aim your crosshair at any frame in the group.$(br2)$(bold)3.$() Drag a video file (mp4, mkv, avi, etc.) into the game window and release.$(br2)$(note)The video file is copied to config/narutoloading-sources/ before being registered.$()

pages.title: Two-Corner Algorithm
pages.text: DragIt treats the targeted frame as the $(bold)left-bottom corner$(). It then uses $(bold)ItemFrameLocator$() to find the opposite $(bold)right-bottom corner$():$(br2)• For horizontal-facing screens, it scans clockwise and counter-clockwise, picking the farther end.$(br)• For up/down-facing screens, it finds the two closest edge endpoints relative to the player's position.

pages.title: Screen Construction
pages.text: Once both corner frames are identified, DragIt calls NarutoLoading's $(bold)ServerScreenChecker$() API to build an $(bold)InWorldScreen$() object with the video path set. It then broadcasts a $(bold)ScreenLifePacket$() to all online players.$(br2)NarutoLoading takes full control of subsequent rendering and playback.

pages.title: Difference from Image Frames
pages.text: A $(bold)video screen$() is fully managed by NarutoLoading — the item frame entities become $(bold)invisible$() and the video is drawn directly by NarutoLoading's renderer.$(br2)An $(bold)image frame$() is handled by DragIt's own Mixin into the vanilla ItemFrameRenderer, leaving the frame entities visible with the custom texture layered on top.
